exposure: Placental magnetic resonance imaging measurements (placental volume of upper/lower uterine sectors, cervical canal length, cervical canal dilatation)
Diagnosis of total placenta previa associated with placenta accreta spectrum
Gestational age at birth (< 34 weeks vs. >= 34 weeks)
cohort: The study included 277 singleton pregnancies diagnosed with total placenta previa in the third trimester at a single tertiary center.
finding: Placental MRI measurements (reduced upper uterine segment volume, increased lower uterine segment volume, shortened cervical canal length, and increased dilatation) significantly correlated with a higher probability of peripartum hysterectomy, and the risk of neonatal death was 32 times higher in those < 34 weeks gestational age.
gest_age: Third trimester (for diagnosis); < 34 weeks and >= 34 weeks (for neonatal mortality finding)
